Why Local-First Software Is Worth the Extra Effort

By Jordan Rivers

September 2026

Most reading tools save a link and call it done, which is fine until the link goes dead, the site adds a paywall, or you are somewhere without a connection. A local-first tool keeps the actual content, not a pointer to it, so it still works when none of those things are true anymore.

The tradeoff is real: extraction has to be good enough that the saved copy is worth reading later, and full-text search has to work without phoning home to a server every time someone types a query.

Neither of those is a new problem. SQLite's FTS5 extension has solved offline full-text search for over a decade; the harder part is reliably telling an article's actual text apart from the navigation, ads, and related-links boxes surrounding it on a real page.
